points.description: States that the median splits the distribution into two equal halves (50% of values on each side / middle value).
points.partial_credit: Half if only vaguely says median is the middle value without the equal-halves idea.

points.description: States that for a skewed/asymmetric distribution the mean is not an accurate/representative measure (pulled by extreme values), so the median is the better measure.
points.partial_credit: Half if only says median is best for skewed data without any reason, or says mean is affected by extremes without concluding median is better.

rubric.notes: Full marks for the two central ideas in any wording: median is the middle value with half the data on each side, and the mean is misleading for skewed data so median is better. Give part marks for a vague or one-sided answer, e.g. "median is not affected by extreme values" alone earns about one mark. Give no marks for wrong or unrelated answers; extra incorrect remarks do not cost marks unless they contradict the main idea.
